subject: Next steps: scoped validation run + evaluation KPIs for Vecta POC
messages:
From: Soren Kline <soren.k@vecta.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: quick sync today — interest in POC

Thanks for the call this morning, Mateo — good to meet you and learn more about Redwood's routing and caching approach. Vecta is keen to validate two things in a short trial: 1) accuracy/quality of generated summaries against our human baseline, and 2) cost/latency profile when serving our mixed workloads (document summarization + short Q&A).

High-level constraints from our side:
- Representative traffic: 40–80 requests/sec peak, mostly 1–4 input documents per request (avg 350 tokens).
- Target latency: user-facing responses ideally <200ms P95 for short Q&A; summarization can be a bit higher but prefer <500ms.
- Budget: POC cost ideally under $10k for a 4-week validation run.

Can you send a short POC plan that lists success criteria, what you need from us (workload samples, eval rubric), and an approximate timeline? Procurement will want a skinny mutual action plan.

—Soren
Soren Kline
Head of ML Platforms, Vecta AI
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Soren Kline <soren.k@vecta.ai>, procurement@vecta.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: quick sync today — interest in POC

Soren — thanks for the quick summary and for outlining the constraints. Attached is a concise POC scope I drafted (vecta_poc_scope.pdf) and an evaluation template (poc_evaluation_template.csv). Below is a short version of the proposed validation run and the KPIs we recommend measuring. If this matches your expectations we can lock dates and get procurement docs started.

Proposed POC summary (4 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): exchange sample datasets (30–50 representative requests), agree on annotation rubric, set up access (API keys, optional VPC).
- Week 1 (baseline + smoke): run smoke tests on hosted API, validate latency samples and correct model selection (and fallback policy).
- Weeks 2–3 (load + quality): sustained load tests with realistic concurrency profiles; batch/kv-cache tuning; parallel human annotations for quality metrics.
- Week 4 (readout + handoff): final readout, pass/fail decision, suggested production configuration.

Suggested success criteria (proposed):
- Latency: P95 latency for Q&A flows <= 180 ms on Hosted configuration with 95% confidence during test windows.
- Throughput: sustained 60 req/sec with median latency <120 ms for short Q&A (when batching and caching enabled).
- Cost: end-to-end cost <= $0.0010 per token (target $0.0009/token with caching/quantization).
- Quality: automated metric (ROUGE-L / embedding-similarity) >= 0.88 vs your human summaries AND human pass-rate >= 90% on a 400-sample blind set.
- Hallucination: flagged hallucination rate < 5% on annotated set.

What we need from Vecta:
- Representative JSONL of 200–500 requests (anonymized) + 400-item quality sample with human reference summaries.
- Clear accept/reject rubric for pass/fail.

Owners and contacts:
- Redwood POC lead: Mateo Alvarez (me) — overall success criteria and readout.
- Redwood infra & cost: Ben Carter — Dedicated pool options, costing and provisioning.
- Redwood ops: Monica Patel — onboarding, instrumentation, and tracing hooks.

If that looks good I’ll schedule the kickoff and share a thin MOP for procurement.

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jan 2028 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Re: quick sync today — interest in POC

Ben / Monica — forwarding Soren's ask and the POC draft I sent. Quick internal checklist so we can answer procurement and confirm dates:

1) Provisioning: Ben, please confirm whether we can give them a small Dedicated pool for the 4-week run (preferred) vs Hosted with scaled priority. If Dedicated, what GPUs and estimated monthly burn (ballpark for procurement)?
2) Instrumentation: Monica, we’ll need trace sampling enabled and token-level cost breakdown in the console for their team; can we add a shared dashboard link?
3) Eval infra: Do we have a recommended annotation workflow (Redwood or partner) for the 400-sample blind set? If so, add effort estimate.

Proposed tentative kickoff window: Feb 6–9 (prep week starting Feb 6). Procurement will want a simple MOP and an estimate by EOD next Tuesday (23 Jan).

Thanks — Mateo
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: quick sync today — interest in POC

Mateo / Monica — we can support a small Dedicated pool for the run. Capacity & cost summary attached (rdw_estimate_q1.xlsx). High-level:

- Config: 2x A100-equivalent instances (shared pool), preemptible fallback to Hosted.
- Throughput estimate: supports 60–80 req/sec depending on prompt length and batching; expected P95 latency for short Q&A ~120–240ms depending on batching windows.
- Cost: estimated spend for 4-week run ~$7,800 (covers instance & egress); with our caching guidance you should be able to hit ~ $0.00085/token in the best case.

Notes on tuning:
- Enable prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts — big wins on cost and P95 for multi-turn sessions.
- We can supply a quantized variant for the trial if Vecta's quality tests allow it; if quality is marginal we can fall back to the FP16 variant.

I'll flag we need a signed SOW or a short MOP for procurement. Happy to jump on the kickoff call with Soren.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Partner Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Soren Kline <soren.k@vecta.ai>, procurement@vecta.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jan 2028 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: quick sync today — interest in POC (final kickoff + MOP)

Soren — thanks and apologies for the delay getting everything sketched out. Per Ben's capacity note and our discussions, this is the agreed MOP and success criteria. If procurement is OK we can kickoff prep on Feb 6 as discussed.

Final POC plan highlights:
- Kickoff prep week: Feb 6–9 (exchange artifacts, onboard keys, set up dashboard).
- Validation window: Feb 12–Mar 8 (4-week run: 1 smoke week + 2 load/quality weeks + 1 readout week).

Final success gates (pass conditions):
- Latency: P95 for short Q&A <= 180ms (measured across five 1-hour windows during load weeks).
- Throughput: sustain 60 req/sec with median latency <120ms for short Q&A (when configured with our suggested batching).
- Cost: realized end-to-end <= $0.0009/token (includes model, infra, and egress estimates in our workbook).
- Quality: ROUGE-L >= 0.88 OR embedding cosine similarity >= 0.92 vs human references AND human pass-rate >= 92% on the 400-sample blind set.
- Hallucination: manual flag rate < 3% on annotated items.

Ownership & immediate next steps:
- Vecta (Soren): share anonymized 500-request sample + 400 human-reference set by Jan 31.
- Redwood (Mateo): provide API keys, test credentials, and poc_evaluation_template.csv; schedule kickoff and weekly syncs.
- Redwood (Ben): provision Dedicated pool Feb 6 and share cost workbook.
- Redwood (Monica): create the shared dashboard link (tracing, latency, per-route token cost) and invite Vecta.

Procurement items we will attach to the kickoff package: short MOP, estimated cost workbook (rdw_estimate_q1.xlsx), and a brief SOW. DocuSign link for the MOP: https://docusign.com/req/abcd-5678

If you confirm by EOD Jan 31 we’ll lock the Feb 6 prep. Happy to hop on a 20-min sync early next week to answer any clarifying questions.

Best,
